subject: problem simulating (scalar) AR process using tsDyn::VAR.sim

messages.author: 35356c7ce6c495ae
messages.subject: problem simulating (scalar) AR process using tsDyn::VAR.sim
parts:
I want to simulate the following (scalar) AR process:

y_t = 0.3y_{t-1}+0.2_{t-2}+u_t

so I entered the following command in to R:

VAR.sim(B=matrix(c(0.3,0.2), nrow=1), n=3000, include="none",lag=2)

However, I got the following error message:

 Error in Bfull[, -c(1, 2)] %*% Yexo : non-conformable arguments
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In cbind(m2[, 1:(i - 1)], matrix(v, nrow = nr), m2[, i:ncol(m2)]) :
  number of rows of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 3)
2: In rbind(matrix(0, nrow = p, ncol = k), innov) :
  number of columns of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 2)

After some debugging, I found the problem is in lines 8-9 of myInsertCol:

    for (i in c[!c %in% c(1, length(c) + nc)]) m2 <- cbind(m2[, 
        1:(i - 1)], matrix(v, nrow = nr), m2[, i:ncol(m2)])

Before line 8, m2 is [1,1:3] 0 0.3 0.2. However, after line 9, m2 becomes [1,1:3] 0 0 0.3. This is certainly wrong, because one of the coefficient is lost in the process.

What should I do to simulate AR process in tsDyn::VAR.sim. Did I use the function in the wrong way?

Thanks!

messages.author: 8c45483022d450d5
messages.subject: Re: [tsDyn] problem simulating (scalar) AR process using tsDyn::VAR.sim
parts:
Dear Samuel

You can simulate an AR with the VAR function, although the base function arima.sim will be simpler for you.

The problem is that you are not specifying the input matrix correctly: you should give the inputs in the VAR specification, doing as if there were two variables:
library(tsDyn)
B <- matrix(0, nrow=2, ncol=4)
B[1,1] <- 0.3
B[1,3] <- 0.2

VAR.sim(B=B, n=30, include="none",lag=2)

But again, it makes more sense to use arima.sim() for an AR.

best,

Matthieu
